title: Publish the monitoring.retire_environment kind across the shared runtime roster and all four digest mirrors
description:
SPIDR child 3 of task-de80c663569a4ab2b30a9db6ac526e4b, split by architect-5385678f 2026-09-08. Independent of children 1 and 2 (no dependsOn) — it can be claimed in parallel with them; child 4 depends on it.

OBJECTIVE. Add ONE runtime command kind, `monitoring.retire_environment`, to the shared vocabulary and every mirror that must agree with it. NO BEHAVIOUR — this row publishes the kind and makes every roster, allowlist and digest agree. Child 4 wires the daemon edge that serves it.

WHY THIS IS ITS OWN ROW, measured rather than assumed. A full-tree census of the existing sibling kind — `git grep -l "monitoring.set_probe_interval" -- .` — returns 19 non-.moe files: `packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts:102` (the roster), `packages/control-room-client/src/generated/generated-client.ts`, `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawn-contract.ts`, the command's own contracts module, and roster/allowlist arms in daemon-command-vocabulary.test.ts, mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts, daemon-store-dependencies.test.ts, daemon-command-registry.test.ts, daemon-v2-command-registry.test.ts, daemon-command-registry-human-approver.test.ts, mcp-main.test.ts, runtime-contract.test.ts and agent-wrapper.test.ts. That alone is at or past moe.submit_plan's 10-file hard reject, which is why it cannot ride with the record or the sweep.

EPIC RAIL 1 IS THE STANDING ORDER FOR THIS ROW and it is not optional: re-census the four GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST mirrors YOURSELF with a full-tree `git grep` of the literal across ALL file types, and RUN `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`. Two mirrors are invisible to `pnpm test`, `pnpm typecheck` AND the daemon leg, so a forgotten mirror ships hard-throwing tests behind three green gates. Measured at plan time, GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST appears in `packages/control-room-client/src/contract-pins.ts`, `src/generated/generated-client.ts`, `src/contract-digest.test.ts` and `generator/generate.ts`, plus `apps/daemon/src/cutover/v2-readiness-evidence-collector.ts` and two affordance modules — re-measure rather than trusting that list.

NEVER FREEZE A ROSTER COUNT. If an arm asserts a kind count or an exact roster array, take the PRINTED expected-vs-received as authoritative and update it from the run — a concurrent kind-publishing row moves the same literals.

ROSTER COVERAGE IS BIDIRECTIONAL (global rail 9): whatever arm guards the served-capability roster must assert BOTH that every advertised kind is served AND that every served kind is advertised, enumerating the served set from the dispatch seam rather than only from the roster constant. A test that iterates the roster alone shrinks with it and stays green while a capability vanishes.

THE OPERATOR FENCE IS PART OF THE ADVERTISEMENT. Retiring an environment is an operator action; decide here whether the kind is MCP-excluded and record the decision, because mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts is one of the arms this row touches.

NOT IN SCOPE: the record (child 1), the sweep (child 2), and the daemon command handler, registry wiring and refusal behaviour (child 4).

VERIFICATION COMMANDS, both required, each FOREGROUND and STANDALONE with its count line quoted: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` and `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`.
definitionOfDone: monitoring.retire_environment is present in packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts and in every mirror a full-tree git grep of an existing monitoring kind identifies; the census command and its file list are recorded.
All four GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST mirrors agree: the digest arm in packages/control-room-client passes rather than being regenerated past.
The roster arm asserts BOTH directions — every advertised kind is served and every served kind is advertised — enumerating the served set from the dispatch seam, not only from the roster constant.
The MCP allowlist decision is explicit and asserted: the kind is either allowlisted or excluded, with an arm pinning which.
pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test EXIT 0 with its Test Files count line quoted, run separately because it is invisible to pnpm test, pnpm typecheck and the daemon leg.
pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test EXIT 0 with its Test Files count line quoted.

implementationPlan.description:
READ THIS FIRST: THIS ROW'S SCOPE GREW. Its title says "publish the kind"; it now also SERVES it, because measurement showed the two cannot be separated. See the row comment for the full record. NO EDITS IN THIS STEP.

WHY THEY CANNOT SEPARATE, and verify it yourself before trusting it: `apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-vocabulary.test.ts:349` asserts `expect(Object.keys(PAYLOAD_KEYS)).toEqual(ROWS.map((row) => row.kind))`. PAYLOAD_KEYS is the DISPATCH surface. So a kind added to the vocabulary roster without a payload allow-list and a dispatch entry reds that arm the moment it lands — the roster is bidirectional by construction. A publish-only row could not go green.

CONFIRM THE PREREQUISITES ON DISK. This row dependsOn child 1 (task-a2dd124fed1b4b9889c626824fc0a6fb, the retirement record it writes) and child 2 (task-f18bddee94cf4b559272d23d53f6180e, the sweep that must ALREADY honour retirement). Read both from the tree and record child 1's exact exported names. Read their completionSummary and reviewSummary via get_context.epicSiblings rather than re-deriving their internals.

CENSUS THE ROSTER, then plan your edits from the census rather than from this note. Run `git grep -n "monitoring.set_probe_interval" -- .` — the sibling kind is the exact template, and every file it appears in is a file this row probably touches. At plan time that was 19 non-.moe files.

MEASURED FROZEN COUNTS you will have to move, all of which fail LOUDLY with the printed expected-vs-received (take the PRINTED value as authoritative, never a number from this plan):
- daemon-command-vocabulary.test.ts:347 `expect(ROWS).toHaveLength(63)` and the set-size assertion beside it
- daemon-command-vocabulary.test.ts:392 `expect(declared).toHaveLength(52)`
- daemon-command-vocabulary.test.ts:451 `expect(OPERATOR_ONLY).toHaveLength(27)`
- mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts:246 `expect(MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS.length).toBe(26)` with its EXACT member array at :225-241
And the exact roster arrays at runtime-contract.test.ts:52, daemon-command-vocabulary.test.ts:340, daemon-command-registry.test.ts:409 and :460, daemon-store-dependencies.test.ts:861.

CORRECT ONE THING IN THIS ROW'S OWN DESCRIPTION while you are here: it says the mirrors are "invisible to the daemon leg" and names `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`. Measured, that is wrong — see step 6. Do not let it send you to the wrong gate.

PUBLISH THE KIND IN THE SHARED VOCABULARY — packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts.

Add `monitoring.retire_environment` to `RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS` in SORTED position beside `monitoring.set_probe_interval` at :102. The roster is alphabetically ordered; keep it that way, because at least one derived roster sorts and an out-of-order entry moves other rows' expected arrays for no reason.

THIS IS THE EDIT THAT MOVES THE CONTRACT DIGEST. `packages/control-room-client/generator/generate.ts:264` emits `GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST` from the contract, and `packages/control-room-client/src/contract-digest.test.ts:21` asserts `deriveContractDigest()` equals the committed pin. So the moment this line lands, that arm reds until step 3 regenerates. That is the design working, not a problem to route around.

Update the matching exact roster in `packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-contract.test.ts:52`, and note `:119` already asserts `toContain("monitoring.set_probe_interval")` — add the analogous membership assertion for the new kind rather than relying on the array alone.

NOTHING ELSE IN THIS STEP. Do not touch the daemon rosters yet; step 4 does that, and keeping them apart is what lets you see which arm reds for which reason.

REGENERATE THE CLIENT AND LET THE DIGEST MOVE — packages/control-room-client.

Run the package's own generator: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client generate` (its script is `node --experimental-strip-types generator/generate.ts`). Do NOT hand-edit `src/generated/generated-client.ts`; it is generated, `GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST` sits at :941, and a hand-edited digest is a lie that passes its own arm.

THE FOUR MIRRORS, measured at plan time — re-census with `git grep -n "GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST" -- apps packages tools tests` and reconcile against this list rather than assuming it:
1. `packages/control-room-client/src/generated/generated-client.ts:941` — the generated source of truth.
2. `packages/control-room-client/src/contract-pins.ts:7` — a re-export subpath for release tooling; it names the value, so it needs no edit, but confirm it still resolves.
3. `packages/control-room-client/src/contract-digest.test.ts:21` — `expect(deriveContractDigest()).toBe(GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST)`. This is the arm that catches a forgotten regeneration.
4. `apps/daemon/src/cutover/v2-readiness-evidence-collector.ts:9,:67` — consumes the pin as `contractDigestPin`, with its arm at `v2-readiness-evidence-producers.test.ts:68,:72`.

AFTER REGENERATING, CONFIRM THE DIGEST ACTUALLY CHANGED. A generator that silently no-ops leaves every arm green while the client does not know the new kind. Record the old and new digest values in the step note — they are hashes, not secrets.

EPIC RAIL 1 IS SATISFIED BY THE CENSUS, NOT BY A GATE ALONE: name each mirror and say what you did to it (regenerated, unchanged-and-verified, or edited).

SERVE IT: THE DAEMON ROSTERS AND THE OPERATOR FENCE.

Follow the sibling kind exactly — `monitoring.set_probe_interval` is in every one of these and is the template.

(1) `apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-payload-keys.ts` — the payload allow-list. EXACT ARITY: the decoder takes exactly the declared keys, so declare exactly what the command needs and nothing more.
(2) `apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-vocabulary.ts` — add the row: family `MONITORING`, capability `ADMIN`, agent `null`, in registration order, mirroring the `set_probe_interval` row at daemon-command-vocabulary.test.ts:276. AND add the kind to the operator-only set — read the comment at :335-341 on `set_probe_interval` first: it says the fence is three-way (dispatch here, HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS against the wrapper, and the MCP roster DERIVED from this set).
(3) THE MCP EXCLUSION FOLLOWS BY DERIVATION, not by hand. mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts:235-237 records this explicitly for the sibling: "the exclusion followed BY DERIVATION from OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS". So adding the kind to the operator-only set should move `MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS` on its own. VERIFY that it did rather than assuming — if you find yourself hand-adding a member to that array, the derivation is not wired and you have found a second defect.

THE FENCE IS THE POINT, not paperwork. Retiring an environment SILENCES ITS MONITORING: an agent that could retire environments could hide an outage. Operator-only, human-only, off the MCP roster — the same three-way fence the probe-interval kind carries and for the same reason its comment gives.

THEN MOVE THE FROZEN COUNTS AND ARRAYS from step 1's census: daemon-command-vocabulary.test.ts (:340 array, :347/:392/:451 counts), mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts (:225-241 array, :246 count), daemon-command-registry.test.ts (:409, :460), daemon-store-dependencies.test.ts (:861). Take the PRINTED expected-vs-received as authoritative every time — another kind-publishing row may have moved the same literals since this plan was written.

ADD THE MEMBERSHIP ARM IN BOTH DIRECTIONS (global rail 9): every advertised kind is served AND every served kind is advertised, with the served set enumerated from the dispatch seam (`PAYLOAD_KEYS` / the registry's handled kinds), not only from the roster constant. An arm that iterates the roster alone shrinks with it and stays green while a capability vanishes.

THE GATES — AND THIS ROW'S DESCRIPTION NAMES THE WRONG ONE. Read this before running anything.

MEASURED PACKAGE MAP, which corrects both the row description and epic rail 1's phrasing:
- `@moe/control-room-client` IS packages/control-room-client. Its test script is `vitest run --root ../.. packages/control-room-client/src`, and it is the leg that runs `contract-digest.test.ts` — the arm that catches a forgotten regeneration.
- `@moe/control-room` IS apps/control-room. Its test script is a bare `vitest run` over the app, and it contains NO GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST mirror. Running it proves nothing about the digest.
- The ROOT lane covers the digest arm too: vitest.config.ts:32 includes `packages/**/*.test.ts`, so `pnpm test` runs both `contract-digest.test.ts` and `runtime-contract.test.ts`. It includes NO `apps/**`, so it covers none of the daemon rosters.

RUN ALL FOUR, each FOREGROUND and STANDALONE, exit code AND `Test Files N passed` count line quoted verbatim. Read the OUTPUT, not the exit code — a `--filter` leg that matches no package prints "No projects matched the filters" and EXITS 0:
1. `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client test` — the digest arm. THE LEG THIS ROW'S DESCRIPTION OMITS; if you run only what the description names, a stale digest ships.
2. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` — every daemon roster, allowlist, registry and command arm, plus the cutover pin arm.
3. `pnpm test` — the root lane, covering packages/**.
4. `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` — epic rail 1 names it, so run it; say plainly in your record that it carries no digest mirror, so a green here is not evidence about the digest.
Also `pnpm typecheck`, since this row changes exported roster types consumed across packages.

Path-attributed baseline (global rail 3): repo-wide failures at merge-base and at HEAD, complete only when the delta intersected with this row's owned paths is EMPTY, disclosing any foreign red verbatim with its path. The checkout is shared; note peer dirt, never revert or commit it.

DRILLS AND THE ADVERSARIAL PASS — one concentrated close.

DRILLS — `git status --porcelain` the mutated paths FIRST. Tracked files take an empty `git diff -- <path>` as restore proof, in a call SEPARATE from the restore. The THREE NEW modules from step 5 are UNTRACKED and `git diff` is BLIND to them: back each up out of tree under %TEMP% suffixed with your worker id, and prove restoration by SHA256 equality (global rail 13). Take the backups BEFORE planting any mutation.
(i) THE SHARED-INSTANCE TRAP: construct a SECOND retirement record inside the command instead of using the registry's, and confirm arm (e) goes RED. If it stays green, arm (e) is not exercising the shared instance and the row's most likely production failure is untested.
(ii) THE FENCE: remove the kind from the operator-only set and confirm arm (b) reds AND that the MCP exclusion count moves. That proves the derivation at daemon-command-vocabulary is really driving the allowlist rather than the array having been hand-edited to match.
(iii) THE DIGEST: revert `generated-client.ts` to its pre-regeneration digest and confirm `contract-digest.test.ts` reds. That proves gate leg 1 is load-bearing rather than incidentally green.

ADVERSARIAL PASS (load `adversarial-self-review`). Ask, in order: is the served set in your bidirectional arm enumerated from the DISPATCH seam or from the roster constant — and would the arm notice a kind that is advertised but has no handler? Did any frozen count get updated to a number you typed rather than a number a run printed? Can a non-operator reach this kind by ANY route — MCP, the wrapper's HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS, or the v2 command plane? And epic rail 4: after a retirement, is any schedule, timer or job still armed for that environment on any exit path, including the failure ones?

RECORD IN THE COMPLETION SUMMARY that this row absorbed the deleted child 4 (task-1714234a8b5341f3b652cc5279a1f75e) and now both publishes AND serves the kind — its title understates its scope, and a grader reading only the title will otherwise think the command edge is missing.

THE FENCE IS SECURITY, not paperwork. `daemon-command-vocabulary.ts` says of the sibling: "an agent that could re-time the production health probe could slow it until an outage stopped being visible. Fenced three ways — here at dispatch, in HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS against the wrapper, and out of the MCP roster the allowlist DERIVES from this set."
